mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, implying lower corporate revenues and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both GDPC1 and HOUST on a month-over-month basis indicates strengthening housing demand, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both increase MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL over three consecutive months signals easing monetary policy and falling inflation, which lowers risk premiums and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in PAYEMS of more than 1% signals significant labor market weakening, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% signals a surge in household savings, which often precedes a reduction in consumption and weaker corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
